extracted.intended_audience: The people of New York / citizens and constitutional framers (readers of The Independent Journal)
extracted.subtask_description: Normative principles and design criteria for the structure of the federal government (separation of powers, checks and balances, representation, and election terms) argued in the Federalist Papers (Nos. 51–53).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interior structure supplies partition of power
rubrics_metrics.description: As exterior provisions are inadequate, the defect must be supplied by contriving the interior structure of the government so that its several constituent parts, by their mutual relations, may be the means of keeping each other in their proper places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the internal relationships of departments so each can check the others; use the arrangement of offices and modes of appointment to prevent concentration of power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each department should have a will of its own
rubrics_metrics.description: Each department should be so constituted that the members of each should have as little agency as possible in the appointment of the members of the others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointments should, where practicable, come from the people via channels with no communication between them. Some deviations are admitted (notably for the judiciary) when special qualifications make alternative appointment modes preferable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judiciary appointment & tenure exception
rubrics_metrics.description: In the constitution of the judiciary department it may be inexpedient to insist rigorously on the principle of separation of appointment because peculiar qualifications are essential and permanent tenure will soon destroy all sense of dependence on the authority conferring them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize selecting appointment modes that secure judicial qualifications even if that lessens strict reciprocity of appointment; recognize that lifetime/permanent tenure affects dependence considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence with respect to emoluments
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of each department should be as little dependent as possible on those of the others for the emoluments annexed to their offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that control over salaries/benefits cannot be used by one branch to make another dependent; financial independence is essential to real independence of office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambition must counteract ambition (checks & balances)
rubrics_metrics.description: The great security against a gradual concentration of the several powers in the same department consists in giving to those who administer each department the necessary constitutional means and personal motives to resist encroachments of the others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutionalize rival and opposing interests so private interest acts as a sentinel over public rights; connect personal incentives to the constitutional rights of the office to make officials protect their branch's prerogatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide the legislature into different branches
rubrics_metrics.description: The remedy for the predominance of legislative authority is to divide the legislature into different branches, and to render them, by different modes of election and different principles of action, as little connected with each other as the nature of their common functions will admit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use distinct election modes and principles of action for each legislative branch to reduce their ability to combine and encroach on other departments; consider further procedural safeguards as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fortify the weak executive via qualified connections
rubrics_metrics.description: An absolute negative on the legislature appears natural for the executive, but may be unsafe or insufficient; the defect may be supplied by some qualified connection between the executive and the weaker branch of the legislature so the latter may support the constitutional rights of the former without being too detached from its own rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design limited institutional links (e.g., vetoes, appointment/consent mechanisms) that encourage the weaker legislative branch to defend executive constitutional rights while preserving separation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federalism creates a double security
rubrics_metrics.description: In the compound republic of America, the power surrendered by the people is first divided between two distinct governments, and then the portion allotted to each subdivided among distinct and separate departments, creating a double security to the rights of the people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate powers between national and state governments and then subdivide within each to produce mutual controls; design interaction so different governments will control each other and themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard minority from majority via multiplicity of interests
rubrics_metrics.description: To guard one part of society against the injustice of the other, comprehend in the society so many separate descriptions of citizens as will render an unjust combination of a majority improbable; multiplicity of interests and sects secures rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor broad, diverse representation and fragmentation of interests over creating an independent will (e.g., hereditary authority) as the security for minority rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent (size) of republic affects security
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree of security for civil and religious rights will depend on the number of interests and sects, which depends on the extent of country and number of people; within a practical sphere, the larger the society the more capable it will be of self-government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider scale when designing federal structures: larger, well-mixed societies are less prone to oppressive majorities and can better sustain republican government, given appropriate federal principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justice is the end of government
rubrics_metrics.description: Justice is the end of government and of civil society; it will be pursued until obtained or until liberty is lost in the pursuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional design should be judged by whether it secures justice for all classes of citizens and prevents factional oppression that undermines civil order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of suffrage must be defined by the Constitution
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of the right of suffrage is a fundamental article of republican government and incumbent on the convention to define and establish in the Constitution rather than leaving it to Congress or the States to alter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fix the electorate qualifications constitutionally to prevent future alteration that might make the federal branch too dependent on State governments or diminish peoples' rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications for Representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: A representative must be of the age of twenty-five years; must have been seven years a citizen of the United States; must, at the time of his election, be an inhabitant of the State he is to represent; and during his service must hold no office under the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set reasonable uniform qualifications to open the office to merit broadly while ensuring familiarity and local connection; these are less variable than elector qualifications and suitable for constitutional definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election frequency: biennial elections preferred
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent elections secure dependence and sympathy with the people; biennial elections under the federal system cannot possibly be dangerous and are appropriate for the House of Representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose an interval (two years) that balances accountability to constituents with the need for legislators to acquire knowledge and experience necessary for federal legislation; historical examples (Britain, Ireland, colonies) support biennial terms as safe and useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term length should reflect scope of power & knowledge required
rubrics_metrics.description: Where no other circumstances affect the case, the greater the power is, the shorter ought to be its duration; conversely, the smaller the power, the more safely may its duration be protracted. The federal legislature's business exceeds that of a single State and requires more time to acquire requisite practical knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set representative terms proportional to the complexity/diversity of the legislative agenda (e.g., two years for federal representatives to learn varied state laws, commerce, militia, and foreign-affairs implications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representatives must acquire extensive, practical knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal representatives ought to possess knowledge of varying state laws, commerce, ports, usages, regulations, the law of nations (where municipal), and internal circumstances—some of which can only be acquired effectively by practical attention during actual service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design terms and institutional support to allow legislators to gain requisite practical knowledge (longer terms, opportunity for continuity, access to public information) rather than relying solely on private study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity and experience reduce vulnerability
rubrics_metrics.description: A few members will possess superior talents and by frequent re-elections become masters of public business; the greater the proportion of new members and the less information of the bulk of members, the more apt they will be to fall into snares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve some continuity (through re-election likelihood and moderate term length) so experienced legislators can guide newcomers and resist undue influence or manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Longer terms mitigate election irregularities
rubrics_metrics.description: With very frequent (e.g., annual) elections, spurious elections cannot be investigated and annulled in time; a return obtained by unlawful means will let an irregular member hold office long enough to answer his purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer term lengths (biennial) that reduce incentives for unlawful means of obtaining returns, especially in distant constituencies where investigating irregularities is slower.
